scenes.title: Casting off from Troy
scenes.caption: After Troy falls, Odysseus leaves with twelve ships, beginning the return he recounts to the Phaeacians. This page imagines the departure in Book 9.

scenes.title: Driven back to the ships
scenes.caption: At Ismarus, the raiders linger over their plunder until the Cicones rally against them. Odysseus loses six men from each ship before escaping (Book 9).

scenes.title: The cape disappears in rain
scenes.caption: Rounding Malea, a northerly wind and the current carry the ships away from their course for home. The storm opens the voyage into unfamiliar waters (Book 9).

scenes.title: The taste of forgetting
scenes.caption: The Lotus-eaters offer food that makes the scouts forget their wish to go home. Odysseus brings them back by force and ties them beneath the rowing benches (Book 9).

scenes.title: Beneath the ram
scenes.caption: Calling himself Nobody, Odysseus outwits Polyphemus. At dawn he clings beneath a ram while the blinded Cyclops feels the animals’ backs as they leave the cave (Book 9).

scenes.title: A bag full of winds
scenes.caption: Aeolus closes the blustering winds inside an oxhide bag, leaving the west wind to carry the ships toward Ithaca (Book 10).

scenes.title: Home lost within sight
scenes.caption: With Ithaca close enough for its fires to be seen, the crew opens the bag while Odysseus sleeps. The released winds drive them back across the sea (Book 10).

scenes.title: Aeolus closes his door
scenes.caption: Back on Aeolia, Odysseus asks for help again. Aeolus refuses to aid a man he believes the gods oppose (Book 10).

scenes.title: One ship outside the harbour
scenes.caption: The Laestrygonians crush the ships trapped inside their enclosed harbour. Odysseus, who moored outside, cuts his cable and escapes with the only surviving vessel (Book 10).

scenes.title: At Circe’s table
scenes.caption: Circe turns the companions into swine. Protected by the herb Hermes gives him, Odysseus resists her magic and wins their release; the company stays a year (Book 10).

scenes.title: A voice at the edge of Ocean
scenes.caption: In the Cimmerians’ mist, Odysseus summons the dead. Tiresias warns him to spare the Sun’s cattle, while his mother tells him of the home he has not seen (Book 11).

scenes.title: An oar above the grave
scenes.caption: Returning to Aeaea, the crew buries Elpenor and plants his oar above the mound, as his shade requested. Circe then explains the dangers ahead (Book 12).

scenes.title: The song he must not follow
scenes.caption: The rowers stop their ears with wax; Odysseus is bound upright to the mast so he can hear the Sirens without steering toward them (Book 12).

scenes.title: Between rock and whirlpool
scenes.caption: Following Circe’s warning, Odysseus steers away from Charybdis toward Scylla. Six companions are taken as the ship passes the monster’s cliff (Book 12).

scenes.place: Thrinacia — the cattle of the Sun
scenes.title: The last ship breaks
scenes.caption: After the crew kills the Sun’s cattle on Thrinacia, Zeus shatters the ship with a thunderbolt. Odysseus lashes mast and keel together and survives alone (Book 12).

scenes.title: Building a way off the island
scenes.caption: On Ogygia, Odysseus longs for home despite Calypso’s promise of immortality. When the gods order his release, she gives tools and cloth for the raft he builds (Book 5).

scenes.title: A stranger asks for help
scenes.caption: Shipwrecked on Scheria, Odysseus meets Nausicaa beside the washing pools. She directs him toward her parents’ palace, where the Phaeacians will hear his story and arrange his return (Book 6).

scenes.title: The secret of the olive bed
scenes.caption: In Ithaca, Penelope tests the stranger by ordering their bed moved. Odysseus knows it was built around a living olive trunk; at that proof she recognises him (Book 23).
